scripts.title: Krampus works for a saint
scripts.headline: KRAMPUS WORKS FOR A SAINT
scripts.text: Krampus is often called a pagan spirit of winter. But when he appears in historical accounts, he belongs to Christian Nicholas customs. Nicholas arrives with figures dressed as devils. And in these settings, even the frightening companion works for the saint.

scripts.title: The postcard that made Krampus
scripts.headline: THE POSTCARD THAT MADE KRAMPUS
scripts.text: The Krampus most people picture today owes a great deal to the postcard. In 1869, Austria-Hungary introduced what is often called the world's first official postcard. Within decades, Krampus appeared on many colorful cards: dark fur, horns, a long red tongue, and chains.

scripts.title: Gold through the window?
scripts.headline: GOLD THROUGH THE WINDOW?
scripts.text: In this painting from the 1430s, Saint Nicholas throws gold through a window. But in an old English translation of the Golden Legend, he throws it into a poor man's house at night, three times, so that the man's three daughters can marry.
